record.title: Critical-State RL selects trainable calls before optimizing multi-turn tool use
record.summary: The preprint proposes diagnosing which occurrence in a multi-turn interaction is trainable before applying a local reinforcement-learning update. Nested sampling holds each candidate action fixed while resampling reward-only continuations to separate action-dependent signal from downstream noise. In a four-cell BFCL v4 multi_turn study using Gemma-4-26B-A4B, authors report that training the diagnostically selected recovery call raised missing-function accuracy from 0.14 to 0.283 ± 0.015 across four seeds on 200 paired examples; training the alternative decision call reduced it to 0.095. In the missing-argument category, the selected decision call rose from 0.435 to 0.473 ± 0.010, while the alternative recovery call reached 0.445. These are paper-reported results, not an independent reproduction.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Critical-State RL uses nested sampling to separate action-dependent reward variation from continuation noise, then applies an update to a diagnostically selected model call.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In the paper's BFCL v4 multi_turn four-cell Gemma-4-26B-A4B study, selected-call training improved the reported scores in the two tested categories while the alternative call was flat or worse.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The reported results do not establish independent reproducibility or general improvement across deployed multi-turn agents, models, tasks or reward designs.

evidence_gaps.description: The diagnostic and BFCL training results have not been independently reproduced.
Generalization beyond the two BFCL categories and the tested Gemma setup is unknown.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported diagnostic reliably identifies which call benefits from training, it could improve how teams allocate reinforcement-learning updates across multi-turn tool trajectories. The demonstrated scope is a bounded benchmark intervention and several applications; it does not establish general agent gains.
limitations: All empirical results are reported by the paper authors; the research desk did not run code or reproduce them.
The four-cell selection experiment is limited to two BFCL v4 multi_turn categories and one no-think Gemma-4-26B-A4B setup.
The selected cells summarize four seeds, but alternative-turn comparisons are point estimates; the paired evaluation uses 200 examples.
Task-specific local reward construction is part of the method and may affect transfer to other settings.
Additional cross-setting examples do not establish general deployment gains.
brief.summary: The preprint proposes diagnosing which occurrence in a multi-turn interaction is trainable before applying a local reinforcement-learning update. Nested sampling holds each candidate action fixed while resampling reward-only continuations to separate action-dependent signal from downstream noise. In a four-cell BFCL v4 multi_turn study using Gemma-4-26B-A4B, authors report that training the diagnostically selected recovery call raised missing-function accuracy from 0.14 to 0.283 ± 0.015 across four seeds on 200 paired examples; training the alternative decision call reduced it to 0.095. In the missing-argument category, the selected decision call rose from 0.435 to 0.473 ± 0.010, while the alternative recovery call reached 0.445. These are paper-reported results, not an independent reproduction.

technical.claimed_result: In BFCL v4 multi_turn with frozen no-think Gemma-4-26B-A4B, the four-cell study reports selected recovery training for missing-function tasks at 0.14→0.283 ± 0.015 and selected decision training for missing-argument tasks at 0.435→0.473 ± 0.010. The paired deterministic evaluation used 200 examples; selected cells summarize four seeds, while alternatives are point estimates. An unseen-bridge test reports a 13.0 percentage-point gain in the selected missing-function setting.
technical.demonstrated_result: The arXiv v1 paper and its HTML report the method, protocol and results. the research desk inspected the paper but did not execute code or independently reproduce the experiment; empirical outcomes remain author-reported.
technical.mechanism: For task-defined candidate calls and local rewards, the method screens for action-sufficiency and reference-policy headroom, samples prefixes and candidate actions, then resamples continuations while holding actions fixed. It estimates action-dependent reward variance and applies the training loss only to the selected occurrence; surrounding calls provide context or consequence without receiving gradient.
technical.regime: BFCL v4 multi_turn, two task categories, no-think Gemma-4-26B-A4B for the four-cell selection experiment, deterministic decoding, step-30 checkpoint and paired 200-example evaluation. Additional applications use logged repeat-call traces, Nemotron and memory tasks with different local labels.
technical.strongest_baseline: Within-category alternative occurrence training under the same occurrence-local RL interface: for missing-function, decision-turn training moved accuracy from 0.14 to 0.095 versus selected recovery at 0.283 ± 0.015. For missing-argument, recovery moved 0.435 to 0.445 versus selected decision at 0.473 ± 0.010.

brief.title: Critical-State RL selects trainable calls before optimizing multi-turn tool use
brief.why_it_matters: Trajectory-level rewards can mix the effect of one model call with randomness from later turns. A diagnostic that estimates action-dependent reward variation offers a concrete way to select where to train in a multi-turn agent, while the reported study also shows that the useful training location can vary by task.
